body:
Same with https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/81021.

The problem is that your character's head is turned back 180 degrees in the default pose (as you can see local gizmo on the bone), which can be fixed by correcting bone rest.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44c3e119-55c9-4591-ad9a-dc5baa46051d)

There are two ways to fix rest:

1. Fix rest rotation manually by DCC or Godot's SkeletonEditor

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/03c21193-94d6-478b-b62a-fa698d543e86)

2. Using Retarget to adapt the model to Humanoid as in Unity and Unreal

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9002c0c7-d26e-4200-90ec-91e67ac342ed)

---

However, there is a MRP specific problem is that the animation actually rotates the neck 180 degrees from default pose as the gltf in the first place; so the retargeted animation will try to turn the neck back 180 degrees. This means that your gltf animation will face the opposite direction regardless of which character model you retarget it to.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed3ecf6a-35e2-4f8f-8524-697b8c9bfb13)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a951fcfc-2c10-4767-accb-e3d3edb090e1)

One way to fix this is to include a t-pose in the animation-gltf where the neck has the same forward orientation as the rest of the animation, and set that the rest pose in the retarget.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a12fa2e-202f-4d75-af0c-0ed19ba472c8)

But the straightest way to fix the MRP is to modify the orientation of the character's neck in DCC (if you use blender, rest rotation is edit bone, see also https://github.com/TokageItLab/blender-addons/tree/main/bone_rest_info) so that it is aligned with the animation and re-export the correct animation gltf.
Works like a charm now. The head bone in Blender had "Roll 180"!?! Thanks a lot for this answer, love Godot!
